correctness.rationale: At round r the in/out color multisets recursively determine all directed walk counts through length r. Descending walk counts are t! times coefficients of the product of truncated exponentials E_{x_i}, with the analogous ascending product. Its logarithmic coefficients triangularly recover low-level coordinate multiplicities \(N_0,\ldots,N_{r-1}\); ascent recovers \(N_m,\ldots,N_{m-r+1}\). At \(r=\lceil m/2\rceil\) these cover every level except potentially one determined by total d. Coordinate permutations are automorphisms, so this proves exact equality of the refinement and orbit partitions. Stars-and-bars and the multinomial formula give class number and cardinality. A one-dimensional rigid directed chain has indistinguishable central vertices at all smaller rounds. Independent explicit graph refinement and exact binomial convolution programs passed on their declared finite test domains; finite checks are not used as the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is the unmarked upward-directed equal-chain Cartesian-power family and the dimension-independent sharp refinement depth, not a new notion of automorphism or equitable partition. Searches in a mathematical finding index, published mathematical literature, and previously recorded claims identified no equal/stronger theorem. Three material primary source comparisons were made; possible earlier specialist results remain a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: Specialized earlier results on directed products and equitable refinement could be uncatalogued or expressed in a different vocabulary.
General graph-product literature might contain a stronger result not located in the inspected primary sources.
The theorem makes no statement about undirected graphs, heterogeneous chain lengths or individually sharp rounds for all dimensions.
No independent external scientific validation or priority certification was performed.

value.rationale: Finite distributive lattices formed by equal chain products are canonical posets with large coordinate-permutation symmetry. The mathematical problem is when local directed neighbor counts recover those global orbits. The theorem gives an explicit all-parameter equality of CR and automorphism-orbit partitions after a sharp number of rounds independent of the potentially huge dimension, plus complete counts and sizes of the classes. This is a structural refinement-complexity theorem with useful concrete classification, not a bare enumeration, routine renaming, or unsupported minor numeric improvement.
